e-9694.knowledge_point: Determining the Equation of a Trendline
e-9694.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/dbc57d2facbcf4bcf3b7617480384ea411d26be05d3fbbcf5edc6a14bc5ae216.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
e-9694.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $(x_1,y_1)=(-4,5)$ and $(x_2,y_2)=(5,-4).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-4-5}{5-(-4)} \\  & =\frac{-9}{9} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-1$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y = - x + b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(5,-4)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-x+b \\ -4 & =-5+b \\ 1 & =b \\ b & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y = - x + 1.
$$

e-9695.knowledge_point: Estimating the Equation of a Trendline
e-9695.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/ad0deee6d845c0241108567ce6b0c744604f1f6f50d9af0405523cd9501a96a0.png)

Estimate the equation of the trend line for the scatter plot above. Round both the slope and the $y$-intercept to the nearest $0.5.$
e-9695.worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/722b5393babd1405c0330e9b4ed08c5030ddf6c69bd8b9e3f6c6d138f02c098c.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $(x_1,y_1)\approx(4,4)$ and $(x_2,y_2)\approx(6,7).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{7-4}{6-4} \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=1.5$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y = 1.5 x + b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,4)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =1.5x+b \\ 4 & =1.5(4)+b \\ 4 & =6+b \\ -2 & =b \\ b & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y = 1.5x - 2.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/1c9f30692222eaaed4cda6b608dcc1ccb01eefd6b5fa7730b5b8bb29c9f528b1.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,2)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,8).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8-2}{7-2} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=\frac{6}{5}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{6}{5}x+b \\ 2 & =\frac{6}{5}(2)+b \\ 2 & =\frac{12}{5}+b \\ 10 & =12+5b \\ -2 & =5b \\ b & =-\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x-\frac{2}{5}.
$$

Notice that the trend line passes through the points (x1,y1)=(2,2) and (x2,y2)=(7,8).

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form

y=mx+b.

First, we compute the slope m of the line, as follows:

m=y2−y1x2−x1=8−27−2=65

Substituting m=65 into the slope-intercept form above, we get

y=65x+b.

We now need to find the y-intercept b. We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute (2,2):

y=65x+b2=65(2)+b2=125+b10=12+5b−2=5bb=−25

Therefore, the equation of the line is

y=65x−25.

content.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,2)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,8).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8-2}{7-2} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=\frac{6}{5}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{6}{5}x+b \\ 2 & =\frac{6}{5}(2)+b \\ 2 & =\frac{12}{5}+b \\ 10 & =12+5b \\ -2 & =5b \\ b & =-\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x-\frac{2}{5}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(0,9)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,3).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-9}{7-0} \\  & =\frac{-6}{7} \\  & =-\frac{6}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-\frac{6}{7}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(0,9):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{6}{7}x+b \\ 9 & =-\frac{6}{7}(0)+b \\ 9 & =0+b \\ b & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+9.
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/fdad2c939372e14617ba4e393037d7f5852cd8114467aa914ccb8963c0eacfeb.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})≈(2,5)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})≈(6,1).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-5}{6-2} \\  & =\frac{-4}{4} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-1$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-x+b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-x+b \\ 5 & =-2+b \\ 7 & =b \\ b & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-x+7.
$$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{9-5}{7-5} \\  & =\frac{4}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=2$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=2x+b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(5,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2x+b \\ 5 & =2(5)+b \\ 5 & =10+b \\ -5 & =b \\ b & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=2x-5.
$$

It seems that the trend line passes through (x1,y1)≈(5,5) and (x2,y2)≈(7,9).

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form

y=mx+b.

First, we estimate the slope m of the line as follows:

m≈y2−y1x2−x1=9−57−5=42=2

Substituting m=2 into the slope-intercept form above, we get

y=2x+b.

We now need to estimate the y-intercept b. We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute (5,5):

y=2x+b5=2(5)+b5=10+b−5=bb=−5

Therefore, the equation of the line is

y=2x−5.

Estimate the equation of the trend line for the scatter plot above. Round both the slope and the y-intercept to the nearest 0.5.

a
y=−0.5x+8
b
y=−1.5x+8.5
c
y=1.5x−8.5
d
y=−0.5x+4
e
y=0.5x+7

EXPLANATION

First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

It seems that the trend line passes through (x1,y1)≈(2,7) and (x2,y2)≈(8,4).

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form

y=mx+b.

First, we estimate the slope m of the line as follows:

m≈y2−y1x2−x1=4−78−2=−36=−0.5

Substituting m=−0.5 into the slope-intercept form above, we get

y=−0.5x+b.

We now need to estimate the y-intercept b. We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute (2,7):

y=−0.5x+b7=−0.5(2)+b7=−1+b8=bb=8

Therefore, the equation of the line is

y=−0.5x+8.

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{4-7}{8-2} \\  & =\frac{-3}{6} \\  & =-0.5\end{aligned}

$$
y=-0.5x+b.

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-0.5x+b \\ 7 & =-0.5(2)+b \\ 7 & =-1+b \\ 8 & =b \\ b & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-0.5x+8.
